want: Match parameter routes such as /musicians/:id and /plans/:id
tried: Used fried-router router() route table
error: fried-router matches exact paths only
workaround: Use its currentRoute and navigate state, with route pattern compilation/matching in dashboard/lib/routes.js

want: Run the evolution gates (node benchmark.js) inside an Orchestra task without polluting the friction log or skewing the patcher timing
tried: node benchmark.js x3 in a task worktree where the composer sets FRIED_FRICTION_LOG/FRIED_CONSUMER/FRIED_AGENT
error: Patcher instrumentation logged ~1,800 'ok' lines (benchmark's 600 patch cycles per run) into the task's harvest log, and the 600-patcher-cycle benchmark measured ~545 ms vs 309.5 ms baseline (+76%), a false gate failure
workaround: Deleted the generated harvest log (all lines from my own runs) and reran with `env -u FRIED_FRICTION_LOG node benchmark.js`: 297-316 ms, within baseline. Suggest benchmark.js/stress.js unset FRIED_FRICTION_LOG themselves, or the gate docs say to.

want: See exported top-level functions (export function createTools) on fried-map's F: line
tried: node tooling/fried-map.mjs on a server module whose functions are all exported
error: F: line is missing: buildFriedMap only reads bare FunctionDeclaration/VariableDeclaration at top level and skips ExportNamedDeclaration (the design doc's expected output shows F: createTools)
workaround: None in F4a; REG: names the enclosing function instead. Left F: unchanged to keep browser lines byte-identical

want: createToolRegistry to let unknown roles fall back to a default role set (Orchestra gives every non-master caller the musician tools)
tried: registry.forRole(role, task) directly; an unknown role returns no tools
workaround: Orchestra's forRole maps role !== 'master' to 'musician' before calling registry.forRole

want: A way to tell parser.flush() lines apart from streamed parsed lines (e.g. a third arg {flushed:true} or a separate onFlushLine), so a caller can cap streamed log lines without also capping the flushed ones.
tried: Passing the adapter's parser straight through; Orchestra caps streamed log lines at 2000 chars but never capped flushed lines, and onParsedLine gets both the same way ('out').
workaround: conductor.mjs hands spawnLineProcess a wrapper parser whose flush() emits the lines itself and returns [], plus an Object.create(ad) adapter view to carry it.

want: createAppServer to accept a fallback/notFound route so unknown paths can require auth (Orchestra answers 401 without a token, 404 with one)
tried: plain routes table; unknown routes always 404 before the auth check
workaround: routes wrapped in a Proxy that returns a NOT_FOUND spec (auth: true) for any unknown path-only key

want: fried-tools createToolHttpHandlers to work directly as fried-serve route handlers
tried: passing the fried-serve ctx straight to handleList/handleCall
error: fried-tools calls ctx.send(code, data) but fried-serve's ctx.send is send(res, code, data)
workaround: wrap ctx: { ...ctx, send: (code, data) => ctx.send(ctx.res, code, data) }

want: a raw request URL under a staticDirs prefix whose dot segments normalise out of the prefix (e.g. /ui/../package.json) to be answered 404 by the static dir, not routed by the normalised path
tried: staticDirs prefix /ui/; serveStaticDir returns false when the pathname left the prefix, so the request fell through to routes (/ui/../api/health served health, unknown paths 401)
workaround: server.prependListener('request') rewrites such req.url to /ui/ so it 404s as before

want: Use rg for a focused source search during the assigned fried-map task.
tried: Ran rg -n over the two owned files.
error: PowerShell reports rg is not recognized as a command.
workaround: Proceed using PowerShell file reads and edit only the claimed files.

want: put a title screen's button inside the element that carries createPointer's handlers
tried: ui('div', { ...ptr.props }, [canvas, ui('button', { onclick })])
error: the button never got its click: pointerdown bubbled to the stage, which called setPointerCapture, so the click went to the stage
workaround: fried-pointer now leaves presses that start on button/a/input/textarea/select/[data-pointer-free] alone

want: a hover colour and a blinking caret for the game's HUD
tried: css({ btn: '...', 'btn:hover': '...', '@keyframes blink': '...' })
error: css() only accepted plain class rules: no pseudo-classes, pseudo-elements or at-rules, so every hover state needed a hand-written <style> tag
workaround: css() now takes 'name:state' keys and '@' keys (0.6.0)

want: draw a 136x42 character grid that changes every frame
tried: one ui('span') per cell rebuilt by the render function
error: 5,712 vnodes built and diffed sixty times a second just to recolour text; the VDOM has no notion of a region it should leave alone
workaround: new addon fried-grid: typed-array cells, a per-cell keyed diff and a canvas renderer inside a ui('canvas', { ref })

want: run a simulation every frame without a virtual-DOM render every frame
tried: calling action()-wrapped functions from requestAnimationFrame
error: action() schedules a render on every call, changed or not, and there is no frame clock or fixed step in FriedJS
workaround: new addon fried-loop (fixed-step update, one render per frame); plain functions in the loop, state() cells only when a value differs

want: save one document under a fixed id, creating it the first time
tried: collections.saves.update('desk', { data })
error: null
workaround: update() silently does nothing when the id is absent, so the game checks .value.some(...) and calls insert() the first time; a put/upsert would remove the branch

want: a setting that makes the ASCII finer and finer
tried: scaling the hand-placed glyph figures
error: every figure in the game was hand-placed glyphs, a fixed number of cells big, so the grid could only ever be 136 x 42
workaround: new addon fried-raster: figures are shapes (ellipse, polygon, fat line) rasterised at whatever size they come out

want: lighting that is a system (lit sides, cast shadows) and brightness carried by glyphs, not cell backgrounds
tried: createLight + shade() with dark quads faked as shadows
error: createLight is a flat field with no heights, and shade() carries brightness on the cell background
workaround: new addon fried-light: a height per cell, normals, point lights with a shadow walk, toneGlyph

want: the HUD, menu and journal drawn in characters like the rest of the screen
tried: the VDOM HUD laid over the canvas
error: the virtual DOM cannot draw into a cell buffer; the player wants only ASCII on screen
workaround: new addon fried-grid-ui (immediate-mode UI in a cell buffer) plus TRANSPARENT/alpha in fried-grid so the UI grid overlays the room grid

want: a modal (the journal) drawn over other widgets to receive its clicks
tried: drawing the modal last so it is on top
error: the scroll region of the panel underneath was declared first and consumed the tap
workaround: ui.mute(on): muted widgets are drawn but feel nothing; begin() un-mutes

want: a hold on the right mouse button that works with a real, slightly shaky mouse
tried: createPointer with holdMs 450 and dragPx 4
error: more than dragPx of wobble turns the press into a drag for good; the game gives that button no drag, so the press did nothing at all (no hold, no tap)
workaround: dragPx may be a function of the button; Infinity means that button never drags

want: a press on each mouse button at once (a game with a hand on each)
tried: createPointer, one press per pointerdown
error: a mouse sends pointerdown only for its first button and pointerup only for its last; the second button arrives as a pointermove naming it, so it was never seen and the first press could be left open
workaround: move() turns a button change into a down or an up; an up with no buttons left ends every open press

want: cast shadows that are whole behind thin things, at a cost that does not need lighting every third frame
tried: createLighting point() with its shadow walk
error: the walk steps a row of distance at a time (2.1 cells across), so a one-cell post threw a striped shadow; three candles cost 5.9 ms at 313 x 101
workaround: point() sweeps outward from the light keeping the horizon; shadows: 'walk' keeps the old way

want: the glow of the few cells that shine, without paying for every cell
tried: createLight clear + blur + addField every frame
error: a blur of the whole field: 1.9 ms at 313 x 101, growing with the cube of the scale, for a few hundred shining cells
workaround: createLighting().spill(emissive, k, radius): a kernel added only round the cells that shine

want: a stone that visibly turns when it is turned
tried: strokeEllipse for its outline
error: an ellipse cannot be turned, and strokePath's outline of a polygon is all - | / \ with none of the rounded glyphs
workaround: strokePoly: the rounded one-glyph-a-side outline for any closed shape

want: shapes given in the game's own units (metres) and turned by an angle
tried: fried-raster with hand conversion at every call
error: every helper in the game's scene exists only to convert metres to cells and pass the aspect; rotation is hand-rolled cos and sin
workaround: none in the addon yet: the game keeps its own blob/slab/stick/lump helpers (a createSpace was proposed in review)

want: a modal in the grid UI that takes every click and reports a click outside it
tried: ui.mute() round what the modal covers, plus the game's own modal() and click-outside checks
error: modality is spread over three places in the consumer
workaround: none yet: mute() stays; a ui.modal(id, x, y, w, h) was proposed in review

want: to test a two-handed game end to end with no browser
tried: hand-built pointer events, a hold timer fired by hand, a home-made reader of the cell buffer
error: the first fake events were tidier than a browser's (two pointerdowns for a chord, moves that named a button), so scripted tests passed while the real hand failed; every consumer would rebuild the same harness
workaround: new addon fried-probe: createMouse (sends what a browser sends), createTimers, gridText, findText

want: buttons in the grid UI that only the left button presses
tried: ui.button with taps from any mouse button
error: a right click pressed every button, Start again included
workaround: button, row, slider and input answer to the left button; region() still reports every tap with its button

want: shadows that follow a moving hand every frame on a fine grid (324 x 124 and finer) without relighting the room
tried: normals + ambient + addField + point for each candle whenever any height changed, thinned by hand to every second or third frame above 30,000 cells
error: a hand moving cost 8 ms a frame at 324 x 124 (12 ms on the frames that relit) and its shadow trailed it; at 533 x 170 the light was 20 Hz
workaround: new relight(): each lamp's share is kept; a changed height re-sweeps only the rays through the changed box, from where they enter it; restore() for the quick lights on top

want: a canvas that keeps up when thousands of cells change in a frame (a light moving over a fine grid)
tried: createGridRenderer.draw: a fillRect and a drawImage from a per-colour glyph atlas for each changed cell
error: measured in the browser at 313 x 101: 4.7 microseconds a cell, 5.5 ms of a 10 ms frame for 1,300 cells, 149 ms for a full repaint; the canvas, not the lighting, was the largest cost
workaround: new pixels mode: glyph masks (eight per glyph, by ink brightness, because a browser thins dark text), cells written into one ImageData, a putImageData per band of changed rows

want: a hand on an arm (a thin diagonal strip) to cost each lamp only the rays that point at it
tried: relight with one box round every changed cell
error: the box round a diagonal arm is a quarter of the room: 2,185 of 4,218 rays a frame with a candle carried at 533 x 170, and the standing lamps swept whole every second frame
workaround: relight now keeps the changed span of each row and sweeps the wedge of directions those spans lie in

want: tests that pass every time for an app that rolls dice, a way to say whether a value drifted or jumped over time, and the errors a page raises while a script drives it
tried: a seeded Math.random written by hand in six places, a largest-step and a count of turns worked out by hand in two tests, console.error and window error hooks written by hand twice
error: the same three helpers copied from file to file; and a thing that moves was judged from a still screenshot and was wrong (dust that popped at an edge)
workaround: fried-probe gains createRandom(seed), series(values) and watchErrors()
